summary: Conservative whole-engine reconciliation of the seven validated stage-1 proposals (generic_runtime_objects_01, math_and_collision_01, ui_platform_and_options_01, vehicle_ai_and_pit_01, vehicle_physics_01, vehicle_physics_02a, vehicle_physics_02b). Output: 5 engine subsystems, 17 canonical type families, 7 state machines, 16 interfaces, 39 function-level dependencies, and 29 compatibility contracts. Consolidations, each evidence-grounded rather than offset-name driven: (1) three vehicle-physics object proposals merged into one VehiclePhysicsBody family - the two identically-named VehiclePhysicsBody proposals plus the vehicle_physics_02a Vehicle proposal, which shares the +0x32BC/+0x32C8 mode gates and the 248-byte per-wheel record array with the physics-timestep half; (2) three proposals merged into one VehiclePhysicsNode family because all three independently describe the SAME 316-byte-stride element array at this+0x134 (count +0x130) - HeightfieldProximityProcessor, CollisionModel and VehiclePhysicsNode; (3) the matrix-row identity initializer 0x00578F76 merged into SparseConstraintSolver on the shared global dynamics-matrix workspace 0x008D2120..0x008D3978; (4) the three VehiclePhysics source scopes merged into one subsystem. The corpus FACT that the live vehicle struct is a single 0x48C0-stride array (base 0x5EC6D8, 104 slots) is the physical anchor behind the F1CVehicle/VehiclePhysicsBody/VehicleControlState split, but rule 7 is respected: those families are NOT merged into one class on offset similarity. All trust is DERIVED/GUESS/UNKNOWN. Contradictions are recorded in conflicts, not erased; per-source unresolved items are condensed into unresolved.

engine_subsystems.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Generic runtime object support layer: counted-loop iteration helpers, vehicle physics-body state, fixed-stride element/proximity processing, large UI control-window construction with per-sub-control blocks, reusable linked-node initializers, and session/scoring struct reset.

engine_subsystems.name: MathAndCollision
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Stateless geometry/vector math primitives (ray-sphere intersection, 2D direction projection, SSE two-point interpolation), a collision-geometry container owning strut and struct arrays with nearest-neighbor queries and destructor teardown, and two standalone global-workspace sparse-matrix LDLT constraint solvers.

engine_subsystems.name: UiPlatformAndOptions
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Options/settings UI platform: builds and owns the player options tree (named category groups of typed 9-dword entries, string-field registrations, default control-action key bindings, root enable flag life-cycle), destroys UI objects through a vtable-installing base-chain destructor, sets device state 18 via a vtable+252 dispatch, and suspends an AI thread under mutex.

engine_subsystems.name: VehicleAIPitControl
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Per-frame AI driver control and pit-stop decision logic for race vehicles: AI tick orchestration (pre-race init vs racing path), waypoint/racing-line following, steering-target computation and lane scoring, driver-status state machine, AI ability drift, and tire-compound pit-stop scheduling with retirement.

engine_subsystems.name: VehiclePhysics
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Per-frame vehicle physics (suspension strut contact solving, swept collision detection, tire/grip force propagation with distance falloff, per-wheel spring/damper forces, tire-model session initialization, steering geometry, vehicle control and physics timestep integration), per-vehicle tire-model configuration data, and vehicle configuration loading (.SVM/.HDV parsing, physics dynamics-matrix identity initialization). Consolidated from the three vehicle_physics_01/02a/02b source proposals.

canonical_type_families.name: F1CVehicle
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Race vehicle: the AI field block (this base, roughly +0x4000..+0x461C) plus the shared vehicle fields (position, velocity, heading, gear, engine RPM, fuel, car conditions) that the per-frame AI tick reads and writes. Per corpus FACT the live vehicle struct is a single 0x48C0-stride array (base 0x5EC6D8, 104 slots, slot 0 = player), which is the physical anchor for this family; the physics/control families in this map are kept separate per rule 7.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues only. AI field block +0x4000..+0x461C plus shared vehicle fields (aiEnableFlag +0x32C8, driverStatus +0x4510, pit-lane flag +0x4548/+0x45F4, retired flag +0x4410, waypoint pointers +0x4354/+0x4358/+0x4364/+0x4400). No full-layout claim; per-source samples preserved via source_class_refs.

canonical_type_families.name: VehiclePhysicsBody
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Vehicle physics body / timestep state. Consolidated from three proposals that independently describe the physics-mode-gated vehicle body: generic VehiclePhysicsBody (0x0045A8E0: speed-limit clamp, velocity/angular-velocity integration at step 0.0125, attitude angles, 3D position), vehicle_physics_01 VehiclePhysicsBody (0x004C73F0/0x004E4790: packed-input decode, mode-2/mode-3 dispatch, per-wheel dynamics records), and vehicle_physics_02a Vehicle (0x004E5F60/0x004F1BA0: per-frame suspension/wheel update, wheel-force storage; both gated by the +0x32BC physics-mode flag). Merge rationale: the 01/02a halves share the +0x32BC/+0x32C8 gates and the 248-byte per-wheel record array (0x35A0 stride-62-dwords == 248-byte stride in 02a); the generic 0x0045A8E0 half shares only the canonical name and its attachment is provisional (see conflicts).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues split across offset regions, NOT one contiguous layout: body-state region +0x0..+0x140 (speed bounds +0x1C/+0x20, requested limit +0x24, integration enable +0xD0, position doubles +0xD8/+0xE0/+0xE8); mode/timestep region +0x32BC (gating flag) / +0x32C8 (vehicle mode); per-wheel dynamics records +0x35A0/0x35AC, 248-byte stride; wheel-force fields +0x3664/+0x375C/+0x3854/+0x394C; frame timers +0x48B4/+0x48B8. Packet arithmetic on the per-wheel block base is internally inconsistent and is recorded in conflicts.

canonical_type_families.name: VehicleControlState
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Vehicle control and steering state (GUESS grouping, owner identity not proven): maps raw controller input into steering/throttle/brake commands, applies steering damping and per-wheel steering geometry, runs collision/obstacle avoidance, lap/position transitions and torque/brake distribution. Common ownership of the this object with VehiclePhysicsBody is explicitly NOT proven by the packet.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues: steering/throttle/brake outputs +0x0/+0x8/+0x10, offset output +0x20, raw input bytes +0x68/+0x70, collision probes +0xB4/+0x11C, physics-body pointer +0x15F0, pit-limiter +0x1D30, lap state +0x1EF0, torque/brake scales +0x1554/+0x155C/+0x1564, wheel contact +0x15BC/+0x15C0. No layout claim.

canonical_type_families.name: VehiclePhysicsNode
canonical_type_families.responsibility: The collision/suspension geometry container: a 316-byte-stride element (strut) array at this+0x134 with count at this+0x130, plus owned buffers at +0x150/+0x154/+0x158. Consolidated from three proposals that independently describe the SAME array (identical stride 316 and count/base offsets): HeightfieldProximityProcessor (0x004047D0 per-element proximity loop driving VehicleProximity 0x004FB2E0), CollisionModel (nearest-neighbor query 0x00403640, indexed struct copy 0x00403F70, teardown 0x004045F0), VehiclePhysicsNode (suspension solver chain 0x00401340/0x00401910/0x00401C90). The packet reports the CollisionModel name as descriptive with owner UNKNOWN; VehiclePhysicsNode carries the strongest owner claim and is used as the family name.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues: element count +0x130, array base +0x134 (316-byte stride), array reset +0x138, released sentinel +0x148, owned buffers +0x150/+0x154/+0x158, maximum propagated force +0x148. The 316-byte element layout behind the stride (strut-relative +24/+72/+112..+156/+268/+272) is raw-offset prose only and undefined; keep per-proposal samples via source_class_refs.

canonical_type_families.name: VehicleTireModel
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-wheel tire physics configuration object (owner VehicleTireModel): builds each wheel's compliance matrix and stiffness/damper/thermal state, applies tire brand and compound, computes front/rear suspension compliance and attach-point geometry, copies the session setup envelope, allocates and pre-fills the interpolated tire-curve table, seeds wear/thermal session tables, and sets init markers (+0x30=-2, +0x34=3). Initialized by 0x0043C250.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues: init markers +0x30/+0x34, hud disable +0x70, tire brand/compound +0x1458/+0x145C, curve-table buffer/count +0x1CFC/+0x1D08, wear seed +0x1DB4. No layout claim.

canonical_type_families.name: TireModelData
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-vehicle tire model configuration data constructed by 0x004F34E0 (ABI lead Tire_Model_Data_Init, LEGACY): handle sentinels (primary 0, others -1), compound count 15, friction/camber/slip coefficient seeding, four 66-dword physics-default sub-structs, and the tire config path loaded through StringCopyWithBufferRealloc from global 0x005EA438. Kept distinct from VehicleTireModel: different proposal names, no direct call relationship, though both are constructed from 0x0043E050.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues: header handle convention (primary +0x0 = 0, other handle slots -1), compound count +0x3C, coefficient table entries +0x13A8..+0x13CC. Offset space 0x0..+0x13CC numerically overlaps the Vehicle offset space; keep the two bases separate per packet evidence (embedding within a larger vehicle allocation is possible but unproven).

canonical_type_families.name: WheelSpringDamperState
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-wheel spring/damper force computation (0x004E3D00): builds an orthonormal frame from the suspension axis, computes contact-frame forces, updates spring stiffness and force magnitude, clamps forces to the friction/grip circle and writes force components along the wheel local axes.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues: suspension axis +0x38/+0x3C/+0x40, wheel velocity +0x18/+0x1C/+0x20, spring stiffness/force +0x48/+0x4C, simplified-rotation flag +0xBC, contact position +0xC4/+0xC8, force outputs +0xD8/+0xDC/+0xE0. The a2 contact-patch frame (9 floats) layout is inferred from usage, not packet-described.

canonical_type_families.name: PhysicsStateBuffer
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Small physics state buffer object cleared per-frame (0x004358F0): zeroes the 40-dword buffer, frees the owned heap buffer pointer at +0x9C through the free wrapper 0x00587BCF, nulls the slot, and returns the previous buffer pointer.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues: heapBufferPtr +0x9C; the 40-dword buffer itself is the object body.

canonical_type_families.name: SparseConstraintSolver
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Standalone numeric kernels operating on the shared global double-precision dynamics constraint-matrix workspaces (0x008CFBF0..0x008D3B60 and 0x008D2120..0x008D3978) indexed by global row-pointer arrays: block LDL^T factorization and substitution solve (0x0056FA96, 0x00575BBD) plus per-row identity-row initialization (0x00578F76, merged here on the shared 0x008D2120..0x008D3978 workspace; the packet names this workspace the physics dynamics matrix). No instance fields; both solvers take no parameters and return 0, the row initializer takes a selector 0..33 and returns it.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: No instance fields; state lives in global double workspaces and row-pointer tables. Keep the two matrix buffers and pointer tables byte-compatible (see contract SparseConstraintSolverWorkspace).

canonical_type_families.name: CollisionPrimitives
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Stateless geometric/vector math primitives: ray-sphere quadratic intersection (0x00401180, used by the vehicle suspension force calculation), 2D direction projection (0x00423AD0, AI/opponent proximity context), and SSE two-point linear interpolation (0x0051F6A0). Grouped by shape only; packet reports owner identity not proven.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Stateless; the only field samples are vector-component boundary clues in 0x00423AD0 (x +0x0, z +0x8 of the input vector), not object fields.

canonical_type_families.name: UIControlWindow
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Large UI control window object: leading callback/state dwords (+0x0..+0x0C) and byte flag (+0x10), a ~200-element array of per-sub-control blocks (each with a vtable header from table 0x005ACB6C..0x005ACBFC, a state dword reset to 0, and a target/sentinel dword set to -1), tail flags (+0x49A8/+0x49A9/+0x49B0), and player-options defaults applied by 0x004AA270. Constructed by 0x004A70E0.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues; the bulk per-sub-control-block field offsets are preserved in the source proposal evidence without forcing per-block meaning. Per-sub-control semantics (0 = inactive, -1 = no target) are inferred from the recurring init pattern, not live-confirmed.

canonical_type_families.name: PlayerOptions
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Builds and owns the player options / settings tree: named category groups (Scene, Driver, DrivingAids, RaceConditions, SoundOptions, GraphicOptions, GameOptions, MultiplayerOptions, Options, Controls) of typed 9-dword (36-byte) option entries, string-field registrations, control-action default key bindings, and the root enable flag life-cycle. Initializer 0x004AA270 runs under UIControlWindow initialization (0x004A70E0).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: No instance field samples in the packet; the option-entry layout (label, value/min/max/selector dwords, description) is inferred from recurring writes and recorded in unresolved rather than emitted as class fields.

canonical_type_families.name: GenericLinkedNode
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Reusable three-field linked node (data dword +0x0, next pointer +0x4, byte flag +0x8) initialized by 0x004BAC20; used as a node initializer/constructor across directory, collision, physics, AI and network callers.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues: +0x0 data (int vs pointer undetermined), +0x4 next, +0x8 flag; layout beyond +0x8 not evidenced.

canonical_type_families.name: SessionScoringManager
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Racing/session scoring management struct: owns three allocations (+0x8C/+0x90/+0x94), counts '1' entries of the +0x94 byte array into +0x98, reinitializes ~40 scalar fields with -1.0/0/-1 defaults, and memsets the trailing 0x28-byte block to 0xFF. Reset by 0x004BB950; callers include Steward_Post (0x004D4600) and setup readers.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues: owned allocations +0x8C/+0x90/+0x94, counted array result +0x98, scalar default regions +0x08..+0x20, sentinel block +0xE0 (0x28 bytes 0xFF). Owner type and field semantics unknown.

canonical_type_families.name: RacingLineSteeringController
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-frame AI steering-target computation: 5-lane boundary scan, centre-steering computation, lane scoring via spatial nearest-neighbour queries, and overtaking state transitions on the vehicle. Method 0x004270A0.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: No instance field samples in the packet.

canonical_type_families.name: WaypointNode
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Waypoint-graph node reached through F1CVehicle pointer fields (0x4354 current, 0x4358 chain base, 0x4364 third chain node, 0x4400 lead reference, forward-link at +0x114). Holds position, tangent, up-vector, track distance, lateral boundaries, grip/traction, heading and node-id/pit-entry flag. Data class; the packet lists no methods.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues only: position +0x0/+0x8, tangent +0x0C/+0x14, up-vector +0x20/+0x28, track distance +0x48, boundaries +0x50/+0x54, grip/traction +0x70/+0x74, position copies +0x94/+0x9C, heading +0xB8, forward link +0x114, node id +0x12C. Node layout beyond these offsets unresolved.

canonical_type_families.name: TheSvmHdvVehicleFileParser
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Parse .SVM/.HDV vehicle configuration files (0x004F4270) into an internal setup struct (this) and a normalized output vehicle-state struct (a3): line-by-line '='-delimited parsing, named section dispatch (General, FrontWing, LeftFender, RightFender, RearWing, BodyAero, Diffuser, Suspension, Controls, Engine, Driveline, per-wheel corners, Basic), secondary file resolution relative to the config path, and range/setting normalization. Owner identity DERIVED from the LEGACY ABI lead.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Boundary clues: internal setup struct fields +0x08..+0x13C4 (e.g. rules +0x34, garage flags +0x38, wing/suspension loaded-byte flags, engine-map doubles +0x674/+0x67C, drive classification +0x13C0, gear count +0x13C4); the output struct (a3) is only partially mapped (byte flags 6540/6544/6556/6565/6536/6537/6564, engine-scale doubles 6548/6552).

state_machines.name: DriverStatusMachine
transitions: pit-wait timer 0x4170 < now -> driverStatus = 4 (session type 0x7C56A4==7) else 5, then re-arm pit-exit timer 0x447C
0x447C snapshot timer -> toggle 6/0 and snapshot position into 0x4470/0x4474/0x4478
1 -> sub_4258C0; 2 -> FieldZeroSetter and return; 3 -> waypoint squared-distance vs 0x461C -> 0 when farther, else update 0x461C
steering-error accumulator 0x446C > 0x4558 -> driverStatus = 1 (after RaceStartCountdownStateUpdate when gear 0x39FC > 2)
racing-line reset path -> driverStatus = 4/5 by 0x7C56A4; pit-return 5 -> 3 after tier selection or -> 0

state_machines.name: PitStopDecisionMachine
transitions: PitStopBlockingCondition or session != 7 -> not service-ready; when session==7 set RetiredFlag 0x4410=1, clear AIControlFlag 0x45F4, log via sub_4BC060
service-ready path -> tire-compound tier selection and SpeedValueSetterWithGlobalMirror + PostPitCleanup

states.name: Active
states.description: state-18 value 1 dispatched for a2 == 1 when 0x008B8C48 bit 0 clear

states.name: ActiveForced
states.description: state-18 value 2 dispatched for a2 == 1 when 0x008B8C48 bit 0 set

states.name: OtherValue
states.description: a2 values other than 0/1 stored at this+0x34 without dispatch

transitions.action: dispatch vtable+252 on 0x008B89A0 with state 18; record this[13] = a2
FlagSetterWithGlobalUpdate sets root enable flag to 1
FlagSetterWithGlobalUpdate clears root enable flag to 0, then EmptyStub finalizer

state_machines.name: VehicleModeDispatch
states: mode 2 = full setup-data copy + 14 subsystem state machines
mode 3 = vibration path + 4 vibration state machines + 14 subsystem state machines
other modes = no mode-specific body; all paths converge on effect/audio flag derivation
transitions: this+0x32C8 is read each frame; values 2 and 3 dispatch distinct bodies, everything else skips the mode body
both mode bodies end in the common braking/effect/bit-flag derivation and effect-field update

state_machines.name: PitLimiterHudState
states: state 1 = pit limiter engaged (calls HUDElementConfig(41, 2, blend))
state 2 = pit limiter with weather-noise blend, cleared when throttle output this+0x8 < 0.8
transitions: state 0 -> 1 when pit flag dword_7CC368 set, this+0x1D34 != 0, this+0x1EF0 == 0 and vehicle state mode this+0xD0 != 2 (guard:6)
state 1 -> 2 when the pit flag clears
state 2 is cleared when throttle output drops below 0.8

state_machines.name: TireWearModeSwitch
states: wear mode 0 = wear disabled: NaN-boxed max double written to this+0x1DB8 and the four wheel wear blocks zeroed
wear modes 1..3 = wheel wear blocks scaled by flt_8ACF9C over 4 iterations
transitions: read global dword_7CEA5C: 0 selects disable, 1..3 select scaling
when session type dword_7C56A4 == 7, this+0x1DB4 is additionally divided by flt_8ACF9C

interfaces.name: ISubControlBlockInitializer
interfaces.purpose: Uniform per-sub-control-block construction invoked by UIControlWindow::Initialize (0x004A70E0): each member constructs one block (sentinel seed, vtable header, state reset) via stride-based loops and batch iteration (0x00401000).

interfaces.name: SettingsGroupBuilder
interfaces.purpose: Builds the named category path (e.g. Scene, Driver, SoundOptions) under which option entries are registered.

interfaces.name: StringFieldRegistrar
interfaces.purpose: Registers a string-valued field into the current settings group (used for scene file, profile vehicle, telemetry exe/file, GDB filename, player livery).

interfaces.name: SpatialWaypointQuery
interfaces.purpose: Nearest-neighbour, plane-test and indexed-field copy queries over the shared waypoint spatial tree (dword_5EA2C0) used by racing-line, waypoint-following and steering.

interfaces.name: AICommandQueue
interfaces.purpose: AI command-message queue: dispatch of pit-lane/waypoint-set commands (message id 14) and ring-buffer input selection for the AI tick.

interfaces.name: SpatialGridQueryService
interfaces.purpose: Spatial-grid contact lookup and collision-surface normal extraction used by the suspension contact solver.

interfaces.name: TireForceSolverService
interfaces.purpose: Per-strut tire, grip and lateral force computation used by the swept contact pass and the per-frame force-propagation pass.

interfaces.name: MatrixTransformLibrary
interfaces.purpose: 3x3 matrix-vector transforms, rotation tensors, Euler-to-rotation and coordinate-frame conversions shared across steering, suspension and physics-step code.

interfaces.name: PackedPacketDecoder
interfaces.purpose: Decodes the packed per-frame input packet into orientation components, steering bitfields, per-wheel data, velocity short-vectors, floats and subsystem bits.

interfaces.name: TireCompoundResolution
interfaces.purpose: Resolve the tire brand (TireBrandLookup on global table 0x008AD254 with the session compound id a3+136) and then the compound index (CompoundIndexLookup on the brand pointer and the compound selection) into the two base pointers into the compound data used by the wheel force evaluation.

interfaces.name: SuspensionForceEvaluation
interfaces.purpose: Per-wheel suspension and tire force helper models: suspension force split (VehicleSuspensionForceHelper), quadratic/cubic polynomial evaluators, tire force/torque computation, quadratic force model, linear vehicle parameter evaluation, and quadratic force/torque curve evaluation, whose outputs feed the force summation.

interfaces.name: WheelStateInitialization
interfaces.purpose: Initialize the per-wheel suspension/tire state from the wheel index, contact offset pointer, and steering-direction magnitudes (WheelSuspensionTireStateInit).

interfaces.name: RuntimeParameterHelpers
interfaces.purpose: Auxiliary runtime value generators used by the per-frame update: parameterized torque-curve interpolation, random offset and bias value computation, arithmetic comparison/validation, and float-to-int conversion and allocation count arithmetic.

interfaces.name: AllocationAndSystemServices
interfaces.purpose: Memory allocation and system helper services: operator-new wrapper and float-to-int conversion, LCG random seeding, triple-field position query, vertex/particle buffer allocation, direction-vector projection, and config-path string copy with reallocation.

interfaces.name: SimulationServices
interfaces.purpose: Simulation-level services invoked from the per-frame update and the tire model data constructor: session-state indexed lookup, pit-part state copy, engine wear/failure simulation, 3x3 matrix transform with translation, loop-with-conditional-subcall, and the zero-init/sub-constructor helpers.

interfaces.name: ConfigTokenReader
interfaces.purpose: Low-level token/line readers and section-header matcher used by the SVM/HDV parser to decode individual config lines into typed values and to route lines to section readers.

compatibility_contracts.name: UIWindowSubControlInit
compatibility_contracts.description: Constructing the profile/exists UI window must zero the leading callback/state fields (+0x0..+0x10), seed every sub-control block with sentinel defaults, assign vtable pointers from the fixed table 0x005ACB6C..0x005ACBFC, reset each block's state dword to 0 and target/sentinel to -1, zero the tail flags, and apply player-options defaults (0x004AA270).

compatibility_contracts.name: VehiclePhysicsBodySpeedLimit
compatibility_contracts.description: A speed-limit request must be stored at +0x24, clamped against the +0x1C/+0x20 bounds, and, when within bounds and integration enabled (+0xD0), integrated at step 0.0125 and emitted as 3D position (+0xD8/+0xE0/+0xE8) via 0x0054B4D0; out-of-range requests follow the clamp or reset path.

compatibility_contracts.name: SessionScoringStructReset
compatibility_contracts.description: Resetting the session/scoring struct must free the +0x8C, +0x90, and +0x94 allocations, count '1' entries of the +0x94 byte array into +0x98 before freeing, restore ~40 scalar fields (floats to -1.0, indexes to 0/-1), memset the trailing 0x28 bytes to 0xFF, and return -1.

compatibility_contracts.name: SuspensionRaySphereContact
compatibility_contracts.description: Ray-sphere quadratic intersection used by the vehicle suspension force calculation: takes six doubles, returns 0.0 on any miss and 1/sqrt(p) as a penetration-length proxy on hit. Must remain a pure scalar float-returning function with no side effects or callees.

compatibility_contracts.name: CollisionModelOwnedBufferLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The collision container owns pointer buffers at +0x150/+0x154/+0x158 and a 316-byte-stride element array at +0x134 (count +0x130) whose allocation is length-prefixed 4 bytes before the base. Teardown frees each non-null buffer via FreeWrapper_7bcf, runs per-element release (0x004B0170) over the element array, frees the array allocation, nulls the pointers, writes -1.0f at +0x148, clears +0x130/+0x134/+0x138, and returns the prior array base.

compatibility_contracts.name: NearestNeighborQueryResult
compatibility_contracts.description: Nearest-neighbor query walks linked collision nodes (next pointers at +0x110/+0x10C) and the strut array (316-byte stride, entries with type field at +0x12C <= 1 distance-tested), using a signed plane-distance probe (0x004FB6D0). Returns a node pointer, preferring the plane-verified candidate when its final signed distance is non-negative.

compatibility_contracts.name: SparseConstraintSolverWorkspace
compatibility_contracts.description: Two standalone LDLT solvers factor global double constraint-matrix workspaces (0x008CFBF0..0x008D3B60 and 0x008D2120..0x008D3978) indexed by global row-pointer arrays (0x008D3988..0x008D3A24 and 0x008D3B68..0x008D3BF0); both take no parameters and return 0. A replacement must keep these global buffers and pointer tables byte-compatible.

compatibility_contracts.name: UIObjectLifetime
compatibility_contracts.description: UI object destruction must install vtable 0x005AC830 at this+0x0, chain to the base UI destructor (0x00485EB0), and when the flag argument has bit 0 set free the object allocation via FreeWrapper_7bcf; the call still returns this.

compatibility_contracts.name: DeviceState18Set
compatibility_contracts.description: Setting device state 18 for a2 0/1 must dispatch through vtable+252 on the object at global 0x008B89A0 (state 18, value 0 / 1-or-2 depending on bit 0 of global byte 0x008B8C48), skip when a2 == -1 or equals the last applied value, and record the last applied value at this+0x34.

compatibility_contracts.name: PlayerOptionsTreeLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The options/settings tree is populated as named category groups (Scene, Driver, DrivingAids, RaceConditions, SoundOptions, GraphicOptions, GameOptions, MultiplayerOptions, Options, Controls); each option entry is a 9-dword (36-byte) group holding a label, value/min/max/selector dwords and a description string; indexed lists use 7-entry loops with per-index formatted names; all control actions are bound to default key codes; the root enable flag is set to 1 at start and cleared to 0 at end.

compatibility_contracts.name: ControlOutputCommitContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Every AI tick path must write committed control outputs into the input fields this+0x3580 (throttle), this+0x3584 (brake), this+0x357C (steering) before returning; the racing fallthrough writes neutral (0, 1.0, 0). A replacement executable must preserve this commit location and neutrality.

compatibility_contracts.name: DriverStatusContract
compatibility_contracts.description: driverStatus at this+0x4510 must keep the documented 0..7 semantics: pit entry forces 4 or 5 (session type 0x7C56A4==7 selects 4), 6 is follow-target steering, 7 stops the car until Speed<0.2, and the racing-line reset forces 4/5 by the same session-type rule.

compatibility_contracts.name: AIEnableGateContract
compatibility_contracts.description: aiEnableFlag at this+0x32C8 gates the whole AI tick: AIMainUpdate returns immediately when >1, and the racing tick re-checks obj+0x32C8==1. A replacement must preserve both guards.

compatibility_contracts.name: PitLaneFlagContract
compatibility_contracts.description: PitLaneRouteFlag this+0x4548 and the pit-lane byte this+0x45F4 steer the pit-box/pit-lane steering overrides in computeSteeringTarget and gate the pre-race init path in AIMainUpdate; PitStopDecisionTireCompound sets 0x4548=1 on entry.

compatibility_contracts.name: WaypointTreeContract
compatibility_contracts.description: The waypoint spatial tree dword_5EA2C0 and its count/global neighbours (0x5EA2CC, 0x5EA2D0) back the nearest-neighbour queries; waypoint node id at +0x12C and the set selector this+0x4550 drive pit-lane command dispatch (message id 14).

compatibility_contracts.name: SessionPhaseContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Global session type dword_7C56A4 and phase dword_7C56A8 select the driver-status pit values, the countdown/launch ramp (dword_5C30E0 / dword_5C3144 tables, global byte_5C3160), the ability drift, and the retirement path; simulation time dbl_8AFEA0 is the shared clock for all timers.

compatibility_contracts.name: RetiredFlagContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Retirement sets RetiredFlag at this+0x4410 and clears AIControlFlag at this+0x45F4, then logs through sub_4BC060; AIDriverStructInit clears both when a session (re)starts.

compatibility_contracts.name: SuspensionStrutArrayLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The vehicle physics node exposes a suspension strut array at this+0x134 with stride 316 bytes and element count this+0x130. Per strut the solver writes contact state (penetration depths at +112/+116, gravity-compensated contact force at +120/+124/+128), force propagation results at +136/+140 and a candidate force slot at +144, reads the wheel position at +148/+152/+156 and travel scale at +24, and requires linked-node (+268) and contact-feature (+272) pointers to be non-null for contact processing. VehicleSuspensionForceCalculation / SweptSuspensionCollisionDetection / PhysicsNodePropagationWithDistanceFalloff all share this array and per-strut ABI.

compatibility_contracts.name: PhysicsStateBufferClearContract
compatibility_contracts.description: PhysicsBufferClear zeroes dwords 0..38 of the 40-dword buffer on the this object, frees the pointer stored at +0x9C through the free wrapper (0x00587BCF) and nulls it, returning the previous pointer (or 0). Callers are ConstructorStub (004353F0), SuspensionSetupSectionReader (00435410) and WheelDynamicsInit (0043E230), so the buffer is reset during vehicle/tire construction and wheel-dynamics initialization.

compatibility_contracts.name: WheelDynamicsRecordArrayLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The vehicle physics body owns four wheel-dynamics records at this+0x35A0 with stride 62 dwords. VehiclePhysicsTimeStep stores per-wheel force values at this+0x35BC + i*62 dwords (mode 2), while WheelStateReset re-initializes the records each frame, setting identity 1.0 at record-relative indices 22/23/39 and zeroing the leading accumulator entries, and the first-frame guard this+0x32BC drives WheelDynamicsInit(0x007C7428).

compatibility_contracts.name: PackedInputPacketFormat
compatibility_contracts.description: Per-frame vehicle input arrives as a packed packet: the region at packet+8 encodes orientation components, a steering bitfield, per-wheel data, a velocity short-vector, floats and subsystem bits decoded by the helper family 0x004B2420..0x004B2AD0. Auxiliary words at packet+52/+56/+59 carry flags: packet+52 bit 0x80 -> byte this+0x1069, packet+56 bits 0x8000000/0x4000000/0x2000000 -> braking byte this+0x105D and effect bytes this+0x1065/0x1067, and packet+59 bit 1 -> byte this+0x4024.

compatibility_contracts.name: VehicleSessionInitMarkers
compatibility_contracts.description: TireModelFullInitialize ends a session by setting this+0x30 = -2 and this+0x34 = 3 with this+0x38/+0x3C zeroed. VehicleMainPhysicsUpdate reads this+0x30 for the position-change state machine, and VehiclePhysicsTimeStep branches on the vehicle mode this+0x32C8. A replacement must preserve these sentinel semantics across tire-model init, control-state updates and the physics timestep.

compatibility_contracts.name: PerWheelStateBlockLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: Four per-wheel state blocks of 248-byte stride on the vehicle object (base 0x35AC). The wheel-force field sits at block-relative offset 0x24 (absolute 0x3664/0x375C/0x3854/0x394C): SetWheelForceParameters stores four per-wheel force parameters there, and the per-frame update initializes and reads the same block layout. A replacement must preserve the stride and the block-relative offsets.

compatibility_contracts.name: ContactPointOutputBuffer
compatibility_contracts.description: The 13-point contact-position output buffer at vehicle+0x3AB8 (stride 12 bytes) is computed each frame, copied into the 28-byte-stride wheel output array at +0x1078, and consumed by the vertex/particle buffer allocation; the bounding radius is tracked at +0x3B6C with +0x3B70 = +0x3B6C + 0.1. A replacement must produce all 13 points and publish them to +0x1078.

compatibility_contracts.name: PhysicsModeGate
compatibility_contracts.description: The flag at vehicle+0x32BC gates two paths: non-zero enables the per-frame suspension body-offset override and the wheel-force field-storage path in SetWheelForceParameters; zero disables the override and routes the same four parameters to a direct rigid-body force/torque application using the dbl_7C7428 scalar as the inertia-tensor argument. A replacement must preserve this gate's effect on both consumers.

compatibility_contracts.name: SessionWheelRecordReturnPointer
compatibility_contracts.description: UpdateSuspensionAndWheelPhysics returns a pointer advanced through four per-wheel 33-double records starting at session+5200 (plus the axis blocks at session+5336/+5864). The caller 0x004E45B0 (LargeConfigFunctionWithPhysicsConstants) uses the returned advanced pointer; a replacement must reproduce the pointer arithmetic.

compatibility_contracts.name: TireModelDataHandleConvention
compatibility_contracts.description: The tire model data object's header uses handle sentinels (primary field 0, other handle slots -1), a compound count of 15, and alternating sentinel/zero handle pairs. Its config path is passed through StringCopyWithBufferRealloc from the global buffer 0x005EA438. A replacement must preserve the handle convention and the config-loading call.

compatibility_contracts.name: SvmHdvConfigFileFormat
compatibility_contracts.description: Line-based '='-delimited configuration files with named sections (General, FrontWing, LeftFender, RightFender, RearWing, BodyAero, Diffuser, Suspension, Controls, Engine, Driveline, Frontleft/Frontright/Rearleft/Rearright, Basic). Recognized header keywords include Setting/Notes/Downforce/Balance/Ride/Gearing/Custom/Symmetric. In non-server sessions a file with no recognized header is rejected as an illegal .SVM file. A replacement executable must preserve '=' delimiter handling, section dispatch, and the rejection path.

compatibility_contracts.name: PhysicsMatrixRowIdentity
compatibility_contracts.description: 0x00578F76 must set exactly one row of the double-precision dynamics matrix to an identity row (diagonal element 1.0, all other stored elements of that row 0.0), selected by argument 0..33, and return the selector argument unchanged on every path.

conflicts.subject: Vehicle offset +0x32C8: aiEnableFlag vs vehicleMode
alternatives: vehicle_ai_and_pit_01 F1CVehicle: aiEnableFlag at this+0x32C8 (DERIVED), gates AIMainUpdate (returns when >1)
vehicle_physics_01 VehiclePhysicsBody: vehicleMode at this+0x32C8 (DERIVED), branches mode 2/3 in VehiclePhysicsTimeStep
conflicts.resolution: Both functions read the same offset of what the corpus FACT identifies as the same 0x48C0-stride vehicle struct. Either the AI proposal and the physics proposal name one shared field differently, or one view is mislabeled. Not resolvable from packet evidence; recorded, not merged into one semantic.

conflicts.subject: Vehicle offset +0x32BC: wheelDynamicsInitFlag vs physicsModeFlag
alternatives: vehicle_physics_01 VehiclePhysicsBody: first-frame wheel-dynamics init guard
vehicle_physics_02a Vehicle: physics-mode flag gating SetWheelForceParameters and the body-offset override
conflicts.resolution: Same offset, same vehicle, complementary-looking roles (init guard vs mode gate) but incompatible names. This is the strongest shared-offset pair across the two physics proposals and the basis for merging them into one VehiclePhysicsBody family; the exact flag semantics remain unresolved.

conflicts.subject: Vehicle offset +0xD0: integration_enabled vs vehicle state mode
alternatives: generic_runtime_objects_01 VehiclePhysicsBody (0x0045A8E0): +0xD0 integration_enabled, gates velocity/angular-velocity integration
vehicle_physics_01 VehicleControlState PitLimiterHudState: +0xD0 vehicle state mode, must != 2 for pit-limiter engagement
conflicts.resolution: Same offset read by two families (the provisional VehiclePhysicsBody member 0x0045A8E0 and VehicleControlState). Underscores that the VehiclePhysicsBody/VehicleControlState split is a naming partition of one physical struct, not proven ownership. Left unresolved.

conflicts.subject: The 316-byte-stride array at this+0x130/+0x134: three owner names
alternatives: HeightfieldProximityProcessor (GUESS): element table driven by 0x004047D0
CollisionModel (DERIVED, owner UNKNOWN per packet): strut/struct container + nearest-neighbor + teardown
VehiclePhysicsNode (DERIVED): suspension strut array + solver chain
conflicts.resolution: All three proposals describe the identical array (count +0x130, base +0x134, stride 316) with complementary method roles. Consolidated into the single VehiclePhysicsNode family; the canonical name choice is the strongest owner claim, not a confirmed symbol.

conflicts.subject: VehiclePhysicsBody family is a provisional three-way merge
alternatives: generic VehiclePhysicsBody (GUESS, 0x0045A8E0): body-state region +0x0..+0x140
vehicle_physics_01 VehiclePhysicsBody (DERIVED, 0x004C73F0/0x004E4790): mode/timestep region +0x32BC..
vehicle_physics_02a Vehicle (DERIVED, 0x004E5F60/0x004F1BA0): per-frame update + wheel-force storage
conflicts.resolution: 01+02a share the +0x32BC/+0x32C8 gates and the 248-byte per-wheel record array, so that merge is well-supported. The generic 0x0045A8E0 half shares only the canonical name and no offsets/calls; it is attached provisionally and should be re-examined against other candidates.

conflicts.subject: 0x004045F0 prelabel 'ctor_init' contradicts teardown behavior
alternatives: prelabel claim: constructor/init
raw source: destructor-style teardown freeing owned buffers and the element array, returning the prior array base
conflicts.resolution: Raw source outranks the prelabel; the function is teardown, not construction. The collision container's lifetime boundary (constructed elsewhere) is unresolved.

conflicts.subject: 0x00406640 prelabel 'getter / no side effects' contradicts guarded mutex acquire
alternatives: prelabel claim: pure getter
raw source: compares this+0xC with a2, acquires a mutex via MutexLockWithTimeout(1) on match, returns the lock result
conflicts.resolution: Raw source outranks the prelabel; the function has side effects (mutex acquire). Whether this+0xC is a mutex handle/id or a state token is unconfirmed.

conflicts.subject: vehicle+0x3510/+0x3514 dual role: mass vs anti-roll mixing factors
alternatives: written as the vehicle mass / mass-with-payload (session a3+64)
written as the wheel-block header anti-roll mixing factors
conflicts.resolution: The vehicle_physics_02a proposal does not reconcile the two uses; left as a contradiction.

conflicts.subject: vehicle+0xCC8/+0xD0C dual role: tracked-point flags vs wing transform presence flags
alternatives: tracked-point flags in the 13-point contact transform
front/rear wing transform presence flags
conflicts.resolution: The vehicle_physics_02a proposal records both readings without reconciling them; left as a contradiction.

conflicts.subject: PerWheelStateBlockLayout base arithmetic is internally inconsistent
alternatives: contract claims base 0x35AC, stride 248, wheel-force field at block-relative 0x24 (would land 0x35D0/0x36C8/0x37C0/0x38B8)
same contract lists absolute wheel-force fields 0x3664/0x375C/0x3854/0x394C (spaced 248, first at 0x3664)
conflicts.resolution: The two readings disagree by 0xB8. Also 0x35BC + i*62 dwords (physics_01 WheelDynamicsRecordArrayLayout) implies a different first record. Packets kept as-is; a mod touching these must verify the live stride first.
